Metadata.title: Technology Decisions for Obsidian Memory MCP Server
Metadata.approval: Architecture approved by user before artifact generation.

RuntimeStack.language: Python is the preferred runtime because MCP servers, async HTTP, SQLite tooling and filesystem safety are well-supported and easy to verify.
RuntimeStack.rationale: Python + asyncio keeps the server simple for local VPS deployment while supporting Streamable HTTP, file IO orchestration and testable service boundaries.

Transport.rationale: Private network transport reduces attack surface while allowing multiple MCP clients and agents to connect over HTTP.

Storage.rationale: Obsidian Sync may modify files outside the MCP server, therefore content-hash revision checks are required immediately before write.

Database.rationale: SQLite WAL and a single writer queue provide enough reliability for a personal Vault while avoiding external infrastructure.

SearchStack.rationale: FTS5 is reliable and rebuildable for MVP. sqlite-vec is preferred after MVP because it preserves local-first deployment; Qdrant remains optional for larger Vaults.

IndexSchema.rationale: The schema stores derivative metadata that can be rebuilt from Vault content and supports keyword, structural and future vector retrieval.

AuditStack.preferred_mvp: SQLite audit_log table unless operational simplicity favors NDJSON
AuditStack.rationale: Machine-readable audit is necessary for traceability and verification; LOG.md is useful but not authoritative because Markdown can be manually edited or corrupted.

SecurityStack.auth_model: API key to agent identity and policy profile

profiles.profile: trusted operations except delete and bulk move

SecurityStack.rationale: Profiles limit blast radius when an agent is compromised or issues an incorrect tool call.

ObservabilityStack.rationale: Autonomous agents need precise trace evidence for policy decisions, patch validation, lock acquisition, revision checks, audit and index refresh.

TestingStack.sqlite_tests: temporary SQLite databases with WAL checks
TestingStack.contract_tests: MCP tool contract tests and policy matrix tests
TestingStack.trace_tests: log/trace anchor assertions for critical flows
TestingStack.rationale: Tests must verify contracts, not just implementation details, because autonomous execution depends on stable module boundaries.

DiscouragedTechnologies.technology: Public internet exposure for MCP endpoint
Free-form regex patch as default edit mechanism
Delete and bulk move operations in MVP
DiscouragedTechnologies.rationale: These choices weaken safety, verification, recoverability or local-first deployment.
